sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 of the 1918 Ridgefield Park volume covers the centre of the neighbouring borough of Ridgefield, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. The sheet is crossed diagonally by the tracks of the Northern Railroad of New Jersey, with a passenger depot, a freight depot, a coal trestle and the coal, wood and feed yard of Clifford Mehrhof beside them. Edgewater Avenue West runs down the left side to its junction with Broad Avenue North and South and Edgewater Avenue East near the bottom; Lowe Avenue, Church and Oritan Avenue run from it east to River, and Railroad Avenue, Alexander Avenue and Grand Avenue lie east of River. The largest works is the Lowe Paper Co. paper coating plant in the upper right, with calendering, coating, drying, cutting, packing and shipping buildings, an engine room, a laboratory and a coal heap by the railroad. Public buildings include the Borough Hall with its fire bell tower, Fire Department Station No. 1 on Broad Avenue, the post office in Depot Park, a Catholic church on River, and the Dutch Reform Church of 1793 with its Sunday school beside a cemetery at the left edge. Along Edgewater Avenue are a garage, a bar and The Old Club House Inn, a shoe shop, meat, grocery and hardware stores and storage buildings. Housing is mostly frame dwellings on narrow lots, with many lots still vacant in the blocks between Oritan Avenue and Broad Avenue. A note at the top places the sheet one and a half miles southeast of the Bergen Turnpike and Teaneck Road, and a box records the water supply from the Hackensack Water Co. and the volunteer fire department.
notes: The sheet shows the borough of Ridgefield, not the village of Ridgefield Park, although it is in the Ridgefield Park volume.
Edgewater Av. W. is Edgewater Avenue West today and Edgewater Av. E. is Edgewater Avenue.
Broad Av. N. between Edgewater Avenue and River is South Broad Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Church is Church Street and River is River Street.
The railroad is the Northern R.R. of N.J.; the Lowe Paper Co. works fills the upper right of the sheet.

Ridgefield borough (not Ridgefield Park village), centre around the Northern R.R. of N.J. station: Edgewater Av W., Lowe Av, Church, Oritan Av, River, Railroad Av, Alexander Av, Grand Av, Broad Av N. and S., Edgewater Av E.; Lowe Paper Co. works. 50 ft to an inch, one part. Modern names: Edgewater Av W. = Edgewater Avenue West, Edgewater Av E. = Edgewater Avenue, Broad Av N. west of River = South Broad Avenue.

sheet-22-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 22 is the left and larger part of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, and shows the residential district of Ridgefield south of the railroad, between Hillside at the top edge and Walnut at the bottom. Edgewater Avenue East runs down the part from Hillside past Prospect Avenue, Abbott Avenue and Morse Avenue, turns diagonally to the junction with Valley and then runs down to Walnut. Montgomery crosses the lower half, with Clark Avenue and Day Avenue running from it to Walnut, and a brook crosses the lowest blocks near the scale bar. The blocks are laid out in narrow lots, many of them still vacant, with frame dwellings, some stuccoed or brick-cased, and private automobile garages. The largest buildings are the public school and St. James Episcopal Church on Abbott Avenue, and a fire department hose house with a suspended fire gong stands on the same block. The part is bounded on the right by a heavy line that separates it from the detachment drawn in part 2, and the blocks at the top left repeat the edge of sheet 21 with its matching line. A compass rose shows north to the upper right of the sheet, and the scale is printed twice.
notes: Montgomery is Shaler Boulevard today; Edgewater Av. E. is Edgewater Avenue north of the bend and East Edgewater Avenue south of it.
Valley is offset from Montgomery at Edgewater Av. E.; the modern Shaler Boulevard junction matches the Montgomery side.
Hillside is Hillside Street and Walnut is Walnut Street in OpenStreetMap.

Ridgefield borough, 100 ft to an inch, two parts divided by a heavy line. Part 1 (left): Edgewater Av E., Hillside, Prospect, Abbott, Morse, Montgomery (now Shaler Boulevard), Valley, Clark, Day, Walnut. Part 2 (right): detachment 3/4 mile N.E. of the Ridgefield post office (Morsemere): Ray, Elm, Linden, Maple, Harriet; Grand, Broad, Roff (now Prospect Avenue) and Abbott.

sheet-22-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 22 is a detachment drawn at 100 feet to an inch on the right side of the sheet; a note places it three quarters of a mile northeast of the Ridgefield post office. It shows the Morsemere subdivision, lettered across the blocks, laid out in a regular grid: Ray Avenue, Elm Avenue, Linden Avenue, Maple Avenue and Harriet Avenue run down the part, and Grand Avenue, Broad Avenue, Roff Avenue and Abbott Avenue cross it. Willis Park occupies the block at the top between Elm Avenue and Linden Avenue. The lots are narrow and mostly vacant, with scattered frame dwellings, a few stuccoed, and private garages. The Morsemere Hose Co. No. 1 house, with its fire department note and a suspended fire gong, stands on Linden Avenue below Broad Avenue. Along the right edge, beyond Harriet Avenue, the land is lettered as the Borough of Palisades Park and is not drawn. A heavy line separates the detachment from part 1 on the left, and the lowest row of lots ends in a line marked no exposure.
notes: Roff Av. is Prospect Avenue today between Ray and Maple; the modern Roff Avenue begins just east of Maple Avenue.
Harriet Av. is East Harriet Avenue in OpenStreetMap, on the Palisades Park boundary.
The subdivision name is lettered as Morsemere Subdiv'n.
